views.title: Wayfarer, arriving at Neptune
views.caption: Radiators stowed, bay doors shut. The slot along the top is the shuttle's way out.

views.title: Torch burn, hot fins out
views.caption: Four hot fins unfold aft of the shield on the strake lines and glow at 1,750 K, carrying 1.4 GW of torch heat; the strakes open just 4 m for the magnet coils' cooling. Up to 4 g; everyone is in a couch.

labels.t: Strakes, 4 m out for coil cooling

views.title: From aft: fins and the shuttle lane
views.caption: Looking forward past the nozzle. The four hot fins sit on the strake lines, edge-on to the burn; the two on the slot side stand 1.05 m clear of the slot edge lines, leaving the shuttle a clear lane straight up.

labels.t: Hot fin, edge-on to the burn

views.title: Port side profile
views.caption: 53.3 m long, 9 m across the hull. Bow to the left.

views.title: Shuttle departure
views.caption: Doors stand up at the slot edges; shuttle v1 (3.8 m, Venus kit fitted: rotor folded aft into its spine) backs off its nose port and rises straight out through the 4.8 m slot.

views.title: Metric HARD configuration
views.caption: One 2 m pleat of each strake out: enough for Metric HARD. Field geometry radius 6.5 m.

views.title: Cutaway along the axis
views.caption: Cut through the centreline, looking from port. Water in blue (full tanks).

views.title: Habitat cutaway
views.caption: Five decks, aft is down under thrust. Crew cabins blue, guest cabins violet, storm shelter dark blue.

views.title: Midship section at x = 24 m
views.caption: Looking aft at the cut: C-shaped tank around the bay, shuttle on the axis, slot and doors on top.

views.title: L1 command deck, I4 layout
views.caption: I4 six 1.58 m contoured couches: PILOT and CAPTAIN/S1 on lowered command terrace (0.59 m above L1 floor), NAV separate; S4 shifted 0.20 m outboard to clear slab. Crew manoeuvres capped at 4 g, structure screens at 5 g. Physical suited fit HOLD.

labels.t: Command terrace, 0.59 m above L1 floor

views.title: The pilot's view
views.caption: From PILOT's eye looking at the bow through the crown dome (v0.5.7). Rings: the 60 and 90 deg cones the study scored; the Protective 37-pane seams surround the independent dual ceramic pressure domes with 3.023m3 AOI; occluded sightline test pending. Displays now ride on arms from the command terrace. I4 six source-annulus couches plus low-g workstations, transfer handrails, NAV platform; full suited-body clearance is declared, not hardware-qualified.

views.title: The nose: crown dome (v0.5.7)
views.caption: 37 separate outer protective ceramic panes [1,12,12,12], maximum hoop chord 1.812m, source I4 outer-band pi/12 stagger, over TWO independently pressure-capable ~7m seamless transparent ceramic domes with AOI-2226 interlayer; 16 Strata armour gores close over both. Open here; the gores stow inside the brow ring. I4 six source-annulus couches plus low-g workstations, transfer handrails, NAV platform; full suited-body clearance is declared, not hardware-qualified.

views.title: Habitat crew systems
views.caption: Habitat crew systems: L3's ten 0.80 m WWS-1 ceramic windows, one per berth; shutters close to restore local shielding. The L4 storm shelter has ZERO windows. A casualty travels the port ladder route at 0 g; full structural/pressure certification remains declared.

labels.t: L3: berths 2.10 m, one per person
Berth water ring and floor-edge collar
Port ladder shaft: casualty route at 0 g
Medical bay, opening moved to 202 deg

views.title: Docking view
views.caption: Two cameras with lights at the docking collar give the final approach; the 0.4 m window in the L5 vestibule gives the crew a direct view of the approach corridor.

views.title: Crown dome, open
views.caption: Option C new faceted shell. 37-pane outer debris/thermal layer [1,12,12,12] over two independent 7m ceramic pressure domes with an AOI gel cavity; 16 Strata gores still close above both. Open, the Strata tambour gores sit retracted inside the brow ring. I4 six source-annulus couches plus low-g workstations, transfer handrails, NAV platform; full suited-body clearance is declared, not hardware-qualified.

aoi.name: Adaptive Optogel Interlayer (AOI-2226)
aoi.status: kT 2026-11-01 OPTION A CONFIRMED; FUNCTIONS DECLARED, NOT PHYSICALLY QUALIFIED
aoi.location: BETWEEN separately pressure-capable primary and backup monolithic transparent-ceramic domes; outside cabin, inside 37 outer nonpressure protective panes
aoi.impact_damping: ASPIRATION ONLY; ZERO protection/impulse reduction credited in G6/G7
aoi.survival_rule: EACH pressure dome must independently withstand full cabin differential following loss of the other with gel present, no shock/crack/pressure-pulse coupling through AOI; DECLARED NOT DEMONSTRATED
aoi.failure_mechanics: No measured high-rate stress response; 56 L thermovolumetric compliance illustrative at +20 K; full-shell shock transfer and independent failure unqualified
aoi.cavity_pressure_assumption: EXAMPLE only, not a pressure-control design; each dome must withstand worst case 101.3 kPa independently
aoi.kT_acceptance_required: Independent full-differential failure under filled gel, no coupling, thermal swelling accommodation, pressure qualification and optical/thermal measurement
aoi.shelter_margin_recovery: 0.5t of engineering reserve into EXISTING aft pressure bulkhead, where aft-directed L3-CB worst ray exits. 1.5t bow-armour trial REJECTED (worsened same ray). Exact 36x600 overlay required; no gel radiation/impact credit.

labels.t: Outer centre 1.5 m; seamless inner 7 m

views.title: Berth viewports (v0.5.7)
views.caption: Ten 0.5 m berth viewports on L3 (two tiers), with medical and storm-shelter viewports on L4 below. Acrylic plugs fill the armour openings (and continue through the shelter's water jacket), so the berths and the shelter keep their screens with the dust shutters open.

views.title: Structure: four longerons (v0.5.7)
views.caption: Skin, tanks and machinery hidden. Four 0.40 m CFRP tubes in an X run x 14-34.3 m between the habitat ring frame and the thrust cone; the upper pair edge the bay slot. v0.5.6 had five members weighing 36.9 t; these weigh 12.6 t with the reserve spread.

views.title: WWS-1 habitat glazing, shutters OPEN
views.caption: WWS-1 glazing with Strata shutters OPEN at low-dust viewing conditions: L2 panoramic band, one closable port per L3 berth, L4 medical windows, and suit/workshop/vestibule ports. L4 storm shelter has ZERO windows. All 208 Metric node faces remain flush armour-colour covered discs. AOI shielding and thermal credit ZERO; glazing, shutters and pressure-panes physically UNQUALIFIED.

views.title: Everything closed: cruise at speed (v0.5.7)
views.caption: Crown gores and every Strata shutter closed flush with the armour, as at cruise speed, in solar storms and in torch burns. The hull reads as one smooth shell.

views.title: Wayfarer rev 7 skin: normal flanks
views.caption: Strata over the habitat armour, bare at the bow; tunable flanks in normal mode (light, shedding heat). 208 node faces and the external equipment are drawn from the geometry. Strata's look is a placeholder.

views.title: Wayfarer rev 7 skin: cold running
views.caption: Flanks switched to low emissivity: they radiate 12% as much heat at the same temperature. The heat is held, not removed: about 17 h warms the protected water by 15 K, then the strakes must open. The metallic look is a proposed optical property.

views.title: Wayfarer | Independent power bays
views.caption: Current source's four 0.95t D-He3 core liquid lobes and four dry closure caps; independent C-lite. Native analytic/CG visual reference only: detailed D8 installed BRep cutouts are in the approved Phase1b CAD master. No fuel/pressure-tank or heat qualification.
